To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
insulin stimulates the recruitment of GLUT4 and the stimulation of its intrinsic transport activity.

insulin stimulates glucose uptake by increasing the number of glucose transporters in adipose cells, that the increase in transporters is due to a rapid recruitment of preformed transporters, and that the decrease in transporters occurs with a very large activation energy and a t1/ 2 of approximately 10 min.

Insulin stimulates glucose transport activity in adipose cells by increasing the abundance of glucose transporters (GLUT4) at the plasma membrane and by increasing the intrinsic transport activity of GLUT4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of glucose transport in rat adipose and muscle tissue.
the regulation of glucose transport activity by insulin.
the regulation of glucose uptake in adipose cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rate of appearance of cell-surface GLUT4 is approximately 15-fold faster than the rate of stimulation of transport activity and that the rate of loss of GLUT4 from the cell surface is approximately 2-fold faster than the loss of glucose transport activity.
insulin increases the number of glucose transporters present in the plasma membrane and that the rate-limiting step is the rate of appearance at the plasma membrane.
the cell-surface abundance of transporters closely corresponds with the stimulation of glucose transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the stimulation of glucose transport by insulin is due to the appearance of glucose transporters (mainly GLUT4) at the cell surface, that this occurs in two phases and that the rate of appearance of transporters at the surface is not the limiting step for glucose transport.
the stimulation of glucose transport in rat adipose cell is due to a 2-fold stimulation in intrinsic transport activity of GLUT4 and an approximately 15-fold increase in cell-surface GLUT4 abundance.

GLUT4 is the insulin-regulatable glucose transporter in adipose cells, that the stimulation of transport by insulin occurs with a slight lag and a t1/ 2 of 3.2-4 min at 37-30 degrees C, that the lag period in the insulin response probably reflects a requirement for a slight increase in transporter intrinsic activity and that the decrease in transport activity occurs with a very high temperature coefficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GLUT4 is a highly dynamic membrane protein, with rates of movement into and out of the cell surface that are much faster than previously appreciated.
the cell-surface appearance of glucose transporters in adipose cells occurs rapidly, but that the intrinsic activity of the transporters is also stimulated rapidly.
the cell-surface abundance of glucose transporters in insulin-treated cells is much greater than the abundance of glucose transport in the plasma-membrane fraction of these cells.
